headline: inDrive partners with Pony.ai and Nvidia for 2027 robotaxi tests in Central Asia
summary: Ride-hailing firm inDrive, alongside Pony.ai and Nvidia, plans to begin testing autonomous taxis in Kazakhstan by 2027, aiming for fully driverless operation in challenging winter conditions.
details: Ride-hailing company inDrive is collaborating with autonomous driving firm Pony.ai and AI giant Nvidia to launch robotaxi tests in Kazakhstan by 2027. This initiative reflects a growing global interest in self-driving technology beyond traditional markets.
Testing is slated to commence in Astana, Kazakhstan's capital, in the first half of 2027. Initially, a safety operator will be present, with the ultimate goal of achieving fully driverless rides.

Under the proposed plan, Pony.ai will supply its Gen-7 robotaxis, which inDrive will integrate into its ride-hailing app for operation. Nvidia will provide the underlying AI technology, including its Hyperion platform and Halos safety system.

This move aligns with a broader trend of ride-hailing companies expanding into robotaxis. Uber, for instance, recently announced its own plans to test Pony.ai robotaxis in London and is working with other autonomous vehicle partners globally.

inDrive aims to bring its focus on affordable rides to the autonomous sector, utilizing a "capital-light" approach. This involves partnering with various experts to combine their strengths and deliver a better customer experience.

Nvidia's Hyperion platform is designed to reduce robotaxi development costs by offering a ready-made foundation of sensors and computing technology. This is particularly relevant for emerging markets where cost-competitiveness is crucial.

Pony.ai is also aggressively expanding its global footprint, targeting over 3,500 robotaxis in more than 20 cities worldwide by the end of 2026. This partnership contributes to their international growth strategy.

Kazakhstan's capital, Astana, with its harsh winters, presents a unique and valuable testing ground for autonomous systems. Success here could provide critical insights for deployment in other challenging environments.

This isn't inDrive's only robotaxi venture; they also signed an agreement in December with Saudi Arabia's AI Driver to explore deployments with WeRide technology, targeting a pilot in Riyadh by mid-2026.

headline_marked: [[Half of stack migrations are now written by AI agents]], an 11x increase in one year
headline: Half of stack migrations are now written by AI agents, an 11x increase in one year
summary: A new analysis of 7,302 products reveals a dramatic shift in development, with AI agents leading migrations between major tech stacks like Firebase to Supabase and Netlify to Cloudflare.
details: A new analysis reveals that half of all stack migrations are now being performed by AI coding agents, marking an 11x increase in just one year. This dramatic shift is evident in GitHub pull requests, where agent-opened PRs for migrations like "Firebase to Supabase" have surged from near zero to 50%.

The data comes from howmakersbuild.com, which tracks the tech stacks of 7,302 shipped products. This extensive dataset, combined with a GitHub crawl, provides insights into actual tool usage rather than just popularity.

The analysis differentiates between tools used by products launched in 2026 versus 2024 or earlier, avoiding the bias of older tools appearing more popular. It also notes that many products use multiple tools, leading to shares adding up to over 100%.

While AI agents are heavily involved in migrations, the study suggests they don't significantly influence the initial stack choice for new products. Products launched in 2026, whether AI-built or not, tend to pick similar stacks, likely due to shared tutorials and AI answers.
The real impact of AI agents is in the migration process. GitHub pull requests titled " to " saw an 11x increase in the first half of 2026 compared to the first half of 2025, with 2,838 such PRs.

Agent-made PRs were identified by branch names (e.g., claude/..., codex/...), bot accounts, or "Generated with"/ "Co-Authored-By" lines. This method provides a conservative estimate, as squashed commits or renamed branches are invisible.

Leading agents include Claude, Copilot, Cursor, Codex, Devin, and Jules. Some migration flows are almost entirely agent-driven, such as Express to Fastify (14 of 20 PRs) and Netlify to Cloudflare (13 of 20 PRs) in the latest sample.
